findings.claim: Collecting a formatted type from a referenced assembly in the consuming assembly looks like it conflicts with the deliberate rule that metadata-only types are never analysed or formatted. The ledger entry says that rule applies to the automatic TypeCollector path, and this feature is an explicit opt-in through a user-declared partial formatter, so it is not a conflict.

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] TypeCollector.CollectCore skips metadata-only types with no formatter or diagnostic. GeneratedFormatterCollector is a separate opt-in path and does not go through CollectCore, so it is not a defect.

findings.claim: The README says surrogate members are matched 'by name and type', but the attribute XML docs say they are matched 'by name'. The code also requires an identical type, so the attribute documentation is incomplete.

receipt_plan.detail: Compare the SurrogateType remarks in Attributes.cs with the SymbolEqualityComparer type check in GeneratedFormatterCollector.CreateSurrogateMembers.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: The change implements the formatter attribute with contractless mode by default plus an optional SurrogateType property. The surrogate is a compile-time-only type with [Key] and [IgnoreMember] attributes, and the generator reads those attributes directly. It uses no source-generated attributes and no DataMember support.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: The generator supports attribute-driven settings without a surrogate type. It would honour System.Runtime.Serialization DataMember/DataContract attributes on T, or emit the MessagePack attributes through RegisterPostInitializationOutput, so that MessagePack attributes already present on T are read directly. It would not rely on SurrogateType.
